title: Four unit tests never run: each is shadowed by a later method of the same name in its test class (lint warning F811)
intended: The product's lint gate is 'ruff check . - zero errors' (PRE_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md:139-146; CONTRIBUTING.md:36-39 'Lint before you commit'), and its default rules include F811 (redefinition of an unused name). A test the suite contains is meant to run: CONTRIBUTING.md:175 ('Write the test before the code, and assert the answer'); pytest collects one function per name in a class, so a redefined test method replaces the earlier one.
observed: ruff 0.15.14 (pg-lint-ruff) reports F811 at tests/unit/test_coverage_boost.py:307 and :319 (TestBulkLoader.test_load_networkx_empty_graph and test_load_networkx_with_nodes_and_edges redefine :234 and :245) and at tests/unit/test_engine_deep.py:399 (TestEmbedNodesMethod.test_embed_nodes_progress_callback redefines :367) and :1139 (TestEngineEmbedTextMethod.test_embed_text_embedder_returns_list redefines :1132). pytest --collect-only on the three classes collects each of these names once, and the class attribute is the later definition in all four cases (co_firstlineno 307, 319, 399, 1139; $RUN_DIR/product-gates/lint-r1/shadowed-collect.txt). Three of the four shadowed bodies check something their replacement does not: :234 patches BulkLoader._executemany_batched and _rebuild_indices (the replacement patches builtins.__import__ and passes build_globals=False); :245 builds nodes with a label= attribute (the replacement uses namespace= and asserts input counts); :367 sets an embedder on a fresh engine and asserts the result type (the replacement asserts only that a progress list exists). :1132 and :1139 are equivalent.
remedy: Give each pair distinct names (or merge them) so both bodies run, after deciding which assertions are wanted; select F811 as an error in a [tool.ruff] table so the lint gate fails on a shadowed test.
notes: Test-suite defect, not a product behaviour: the shadowed tests cover BulkLoader.load_networkx (modules 03/15) and engine.embed_nodes / embed_text (module 06). Found by the lane's 3.5-lint run. The other 60 of ruff's 64 F811 warnings were read by name: 58 in tests are pytest fixture parameters that rebind an imported fixture (pytest's usual pattern) or local re-imports, 1 is a notebook re-import, and 1 is in product code: iris_vector_graph/bolt_server.py:314 rebinds decode_messages to its stateless replacement on purpose, leaving the first definition (:269-291) dead; not a defect.

title: VectorOptimizer, a public class, hard-codes the Graph_KG schema, so in a namespace whose IVG Schema has another name it reads and writes the wrong tables
intended: docs/adr/0016-one-ivg-schema-per-namespace.md:10-12: every SQL object IVG creates lives in one schema, the IVG Schema, default Graph_KG, and a user may choose another name (IRISGraphEngine(schema_prefix=...) or IVG_SCHEMA_PREFIX); iris_vector_graph/__init__.py:94 and :123 export VectorOptimizer as public API.
observed: Source at the pin: iris_vector_graph/vector_utils.py:22-26 sets _SCHEMA = "Graph_KG" (its comment: 'The embedding tables live in Graph_KG'); _qualify (:46-50) qualifies every table with it; the reads and writes at :295, :322 and :352 use it; VectorOptimizer.__init__ (:58-60) takes only a connection and never reads the namespace's recorded IVG Schema. The same comment (:22-25) says every method swallows a 'table not found' into a dict, so under another schema a call reports unavailability or does nothing rather than raising. Found by the style review round 2 (style-r2/STYLE-G2.md D-06-14, C-35; candidate N-06-a). Not run live.
remedy: Resolve the namespace's recorded IVG Schema (as the engine does through schema_name) or take the engine or the schema name as a constructor argument, and stop turning 'table not found' into an empty answer.
notes: Same pattern as F-1605 (the sample API's nodes field names Graph_KG) and F-1013 (PageRankEmbedded's unqualified SQL). Severity S4: the class is a maintenance utility (migrate_to_optimized, check_hnsw_availability, benchmark_vector_search); with the default schema it is unaffected.
